skills.text:
# Skill: pdf # PDF Studio A PDF is a design artifact, not a printout of a text file. This skill produces documents that look art-directed: a cover that earns the first page, a grid that holds up across pages, typography with hierarchy, data shown as data, images that support claims, and a contents page that actually helps. **The one rule: never ship the first render.** Build, look at the page images, fix what is wrong, rebuild. The QA loop *is* the skill. --- ## 0. Ask before you build If the brief leaves a real decision open, ask. Do not pad the build with assumptions the reader will notice. If the harness exposes a question tool (`question`, `ask_user`, `AskUserQuestion`, or similar), **call it**. Do not print questions as prose and wait — a prose question usually stalls the task. Offer a short multiple-choice list and let the tool add the custom answer. Ask at most **three** questions before the first build. Prefer questions whose answers change the design, not the wording: | Decision | Question type | Example options | |---|---|---| | Purpose | Single choice | persuade / explain / report / sell / comply | | Audience | Single choice | board / client / customer / students / public | | Length | Single choice | 2 pages / 6-10 / 15-25 / as long as needed | | Tone | Single choice | playful / authoritative / warm / austere / technical | | Visual direction | Single choice | bold type / photo-led / data-led / quiet editorial / let me choose | | Must include | Multiple choice | numbers / charts / photographs / quotes / legal copy | | Brand | Single choice | use these colours / neutral palette / supplied assets | | Locale | Single choice | UK English / US English / another | Use a multi-select question for "what must be included" and a single-select question for everything else. If the user supplied a complete brief, skip this section and build. --- ## 1. Start here ```bash cd python -m pdfstudio build input.md --out out/document.pdf --preview-pages 8 python -m pdfstudio check out/document.pdf --source input.md --previews out/qa ``` That command prints a QA summary and writes PNG previews to `out/.pdfstudio/previews/`. Read those images with the image-reading tool before you report success. If the previews look wrong, they are wrong. `check` re-measures the finished PDF against declared design intent (body size, measure, margins, image resolution, metadata, tags, contrast) and exits non-zero when an error-level gate fails. Discover what is available: ```bash python -m pdfstudio scenarios # 14 document types, with defaults python -m pdfstudio themes # 11 design systems python -m pdfstudio designs # which theme to use where python -m pdfstudio inspect out/document.pdf --previews out/qa --pages 12 python -m pdfstudio images "crocs retail display" --out out/candidates.jpg python -m pdfstudio copycheck input.md --locale en-GB ``` --- ## 2. The workflow 1. **Ask the three questions that matter** (section 0), if they are still open. 2. **Decide the document type.** Pick a scenario from the table in section 5. A scenario sets the page size, orientation, cover style, TOC, layout, running header/footer, and a default design system. 3. **Write the source.** Markdown with YAML frontmatter. Structure beats prose: one idea per section, tables for comparisons, charts for trends, a metric row for the numbers that matter. 4. **Source images deliberately.** Use `![alt](search:plain description)`. One or two images per document is usually right; five is a photo essay. Every image must support a claim in the text. Review candidates visually before pinning a file (section 3). 5. **Build with previews.** `--preview-pages` should cover the whole document for anything under 15 pages. 6. **Run `check`.** It measures real type sizes, line measure, clipping, orphan headings, page fill, metadata, tagging, image DPI, duplicates, and credits. Fix errors before you look at aesthetics. 7. **Look at every preview.** Check cover, TOC page numbers, page breaks, table alignment, chart legibility, contrast, orphan headings, and the back cover. 8. **Iterate.** Fix content or CSS, rebuild, re-check, re-look. Two passes minimum. 9. **Report the result.** Give the absolute path, the page count, and one line on what the document contains, plus the measured result. If the user gives you a topic rather than a file, write the content first. A beautiful PDF of thin content is still a thin document. --- ## 3. Source format ### Frontmatter ```yaml --- title: "Brew & Bloom" subtitle: "A 12-Month Marketing Plan" author: "Your Name" org: "Northfield Business School" client: "Brew & Bloom Ltd." date: "November 2026" version: "1.0" eyebrow: "Marketing Plan" # small label above the title on the cover kicker: "Strategic Marketing Planning" summary: "One sentence that sells the document." theme: modern-saas # design system id scenario: marketing-plan # document type id confidential: "Confidential" # optional cover badge website: "brewandbloom.example" toc_title: "Contents" toc_depth: 2 # 1-3 heading levels in the TOC page_size: A4 # A3 A4 A5 Letter Legal Tabloid landscape: false back_cover: title: "Ready to brew something bigger?" text: "A short closing paragraph." contact: "hello@example.com" cover_image: "search:plain description" cover_caption: "Caption describing what the cover photograph shows." --- ``` Scenario and theme can also be set on the command line with `-s` and `-t`. Command-line values win. If frontmatter is absent the document still builds with sensible defaults. ### Content blocks These are extracted before Markdown conversion, so they render reliably. **Metric row** - 3 to 5 numbers, no more. `Label | Value | delta` ````markdown ```metrics Monthly recurring revenue | £18,400 | target Active subscribers | 640 | target Churn (monthly) | 4.2% | -1.8pts ``` ```` **SWOT** - renders as a 2x2 matrix, not a table. ````markdown ```swot Strengths | Roastery ownership; Repeat footfall; Origin story Weaknesses | Low awareness; No email list; Single-product site Opportunities | Subscription growth; Corporate gifting; Office wholesale Threats | Price cuts; Bean volatility; Delivery costs ``` ```` **Charts** - `line`, `bar`, `stacked`, `pie`, `donut`, `area`. ````markdown ```chart bar title: Budget allocation by channel (£000s) Email & CRM | 6 Content & photography | 5 Paid social | 9 ``` ```` Add a header row to name series (needed for stacked charts): ````markdown ```chart stacked title: Subscriber growth by segment Quarter | Local | Gift | Remote Q1 | 40 | 25 | 15 Q2 | 95 | 60 | 55 ``` ```` Charts are generated with matplotlib in the document's palette. Long category names switch to horizontal bars automatically; values are labelled directly; legend sits outside the plot; figure numbers run in document order. Never put a chart's numbers only in prose — if the reader should compare values, chart them. **Callouts** - `NOTE`, `KEY`, `INSIGHT`, `ACTION`, `WARNING`, each with a distinct colour and weight. ```markdown > [!KEY] The one-sentence strategy > Sell the habit, not the bag. > [!INSIGHT] What the data says > ... > [!ACTION] Owner and date > ... > [!WARNING] Trigger for a rethink > ... > [!NOTE] Sidebar > ... ``` **Images** ```markdown ![Speciality coffee being poured](search:speciality coffee pour over cafe) ![Our roastery](img:assets/photos/roastery.jpg) ![A specific photograph](https://example.com/photo.jpg) ``` Search queries should describe the *photograph*, not the concept: "coffee roastery interior" finds better images than "authenticity". Sourced images are licensed, credited, cached, and embedded, and a credit block is added automatically at the end of the document. **Review images before you pin them.** A title match is not a visual match. Build a contact sheet, look at it, then pin the exact file: ```bash python -m pdfstudio images "crocs retail display" --out out/candidates.jpg ``` The sheet prints an index, title, dimensions, and licence under each thumbnail. When you have chosen, pin the exact Commons filename so a later search cannot drift to a different photograph: ```markdown ![Purple Crocs retail display](search:commons:Israel Batch 1 (640).JPG) ``` Rules that prevent the usual image failures: - Review the sheet at full size. Check the subject, not just the filename. - Do not reuse one photograph for the cover and the back cover. - Do not use a photograph whose caption promises something it does not show. - Every image needs a caption that says what the reader is looking at. - Add `cover_image` and `cover_caption` in frontmatter for the cover; the body search will not reuse it. **Page control** - `
`, or `## Heading {.no-toc}` to keep a heading out of the contents page. --- ## 4. Making it specific to the document Generic output is the failure mode. Do these before building: - **Write a real title.** "Q3 Marketing Plan: Brew & Bloom" beats "Marketing Plan". - **Choose the theme for the audience.** A bank proposal is not `vibrant`. - **Use the metrics block once**, near the top, with the numbers the reader came for. - **Use exactly one chart type per idea.** Do not put three bar charts in a row. - **Break the grid once.** A full-width image or a pull quote stops a document from reading as a template. - **Write the back cover.** It is the last thing read and the easiest page to forget. For per-document design changes, drop a CSS file next to the source and pass `--css custom.css` (see section 8) or edit `assets/css/overrides.css` for a reusable change. Add a `body[data-scenario="..."]` selector to scope it. --- ## 5. Scenarios | id | Use for | Default design | Pages / layout | |---|---|---|---| | `report` | Annual reports, research reports | Editorial | A4, full cover, TOC | | `marketing-plan` | Marketing and business plans | Modern SaaS | A4, split cover, TOC, cards | | `proposal` | Client proposals, bids | Luxury | A4, minimal cover, TOC | | `invoice` | Invoices, quotes, receipts | Minimal | A4, no cover, footer only | | `whitepaper` | Technical and thought-leadership papers | Academic | A4, full cover, TOC | | `case-study` | Customer stories, results write-ups | Modern SaaS | A4, image cover | | `resume` | Resumes and CVs | Minimal | Letter, no cover/header/footer | | `one-pager` | Decision briefs, product one-pagers | Swiss Grid | A4, two columns | | `academic` | Essays, dissertations, papers | Academic | Letter, TOC | | `brochure` | Service brochures, programmes | Vibrant | A4, image cover, cards | | `certificate` | Certificates and awards | Luxury | A4 landscape, framed | | `newsletter` | Internal and community newsletters | Editorial | A4, two columns | | `portfolio` | Design and photography portfolios | Minimal | A4, image cover, cards | | `pitch-deck` | Slide-style decks | Modern SaaS | A4 landscape, cards | --- ## 6. Design systems | id | Mood | Good for | |---|---|---| | `editorial` | Serif, generous, print | Reports, newsletters, long reads | | `swiss` | Grid, Helvetica discipline | One-pagers, data-heavy briefs | | `modern-saas` | Clean, indigo accent, cards | Plans, case studies, decks | | `luxury` | High-contrast serif, gold, cream | Proposals, certificates | | `academic` | Restrained, footnote-friendly | Papers, whitepapers | | `brutalist` | Raw type, harsh rules | Manifestos, culture decks | | `minimal` | Quiet, lots of white | Resumes, portfolios | | `corporate` | Navy, steady, conservative | Board papers, finance | | `warm-sage` | Earthy, calm, human | Sustainability, wellness | | `midnight` | Dark cover, luminous accents | Launch decks, tech | | `vibrant` | Saturated, energetic | Brochures, campaigns | A theme changes tokens: palette, fonts, spacing scale, radius, rules, cover treatment, and chart colours. Changing one thing changes the whole document. --- ## 7. QA loop (mandatory) ```bash python -m pdfstudio build doc.md --out out/doc.pdf --preview-pages 12 --strict python -m pdfstudio check out/doc.pdf --source doc.md --previews out/qa python -m pdfstudio copycheck doc.md --locale en-GB ``` `check` measures the finished PDF against declared design intent. It fails on: - body text smaller than the size the design declares - any text below 9pt - body lines far outside the declared measure (default 68 characters) - text clipped by the page edge - headings stranded at the foot of a page - empty or half-empty spill pages - missing title, author, subject, keywords, `/Lang`, structure tree, or outline - images below 150 effective dpi, tiny images, and duplicate photographs - photographs without a credits block Then inspect `out/.pdfstudio/previews/*.png`. Checklist: - Cover: title fits, no text over a busy photograph, metadata aligned. - Contents: page numbers present and correct, depth sensible, no orphan entries. - Body: no heading stranded at the bottom of a page, no table split mid-row, no figure separated from its caption. - Charts: labels legible and horizontal, values labelled directly, legend clear of the plot, figure numbers in document order. - Images: relevant to the caption, not stretched, credits present, no duplicate. - Contrast: every caption and label readable against what is behind it. - Back cover: present, not an empty page, not the cover photograph again. - Last page: not a nearly-empty page caused by a trailing element. ### Contrast The build runs a Chromium probe that finds text over images and strong colour fields, measures WCAG contrast against the pixels actually behind the glyphs, and appends a scoped CSS fix for non-display text. Display type is reported, not patched: move the headline or give it a solid field, do not shrink it. If `check` or the build reports a contrast issue: 1. Read the selector and the text in the report. 2. For body copy, captions, labels, and credits, let the scoped fix apply and rebuild. Confirm the same selector is no longer listed. 3. For a headline or cover title, change the composition: a solid text column, a bounded photograph, or a different crop. Never simply add a dark panel behind display type. 4. Re-run the build and `check`. A fix that changes page flow may create a new overlap; re-probe rather than assuming. ### Verify the render, not the source ```bash python -m pdfstudio check out/doc.pdf --source doc.md --json > out/qa.json ``` Read `fonts.body_pt`, `fonts.min_used_pt`, `fonts.line_chars`, `structure.lang`, `structure.struct_tree`, `structure.outline_entries`, `gates`, and `image_details`. If body text is smaller than declared, look for an element wider than the page: Chromium scales the whole document down to fit one overflowing box. Fix the box, not the font. When something is wrong, fix the cause, not the symptom: adjust content length, move a block, tune one CSS rule, then rebuild. Rebuilding is fast. --- ## 8. CLI reference ``` python -m pdfstudio build INPUT [-o OUT] [-s SCENARIO] [-t THEME] [--art-direction DIRECTION] [--copy-policy strict|warn|off] [--title TITLE] [--page-size SIZE] [--landscape|--portrait] [--toc|--no-toc] [--cover|--no-cover] [--engine auto|playwright|weasyprint] [--images auto|off] [--preview-pages N] [--no-preview] [--no-stamp] [--no-bookmarks] [--keep-html] [--no-contrast] [--strict] [--css FILE ...] python -m pdfstudio check FILE.pdf [--source SOURCE.md] [--body-size PT] [--min-font PT] [--measure CH] [--cover-pages N] [--previews DIR] [--pages N] [--json] python -m pdfstudio images "query" [--out SHEET.jpg] [--count N] [--columns N] python -m pdfstudio copycheck FILE.md [--locale en-GB|en-US] python -m pdfstudio themes | scenarios | designs | directions python -m pdfstudio inspect FILE.pdf [--previews DIR] [--pages N] [--json] ``` Useful flags: - `--strict` makes `build` exit non-zero when the measured QA gates fail. - `--no-contrast` skips the contrast probe for a deliberately low-contrast display composition. Do not use it to hide a body-copy problem. - `--keep-html` writes the intermediate HTML next to the PDF. Use it when a CSS change needs live iteration. - `--images off` for offline builds, certificates, and invoices. - `--engine weasyprint` only if Chromium is unavailable; expect weaker layout. --- ## 9. Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | Body text is ~9% smaller than declared | One element is wider than the page, so Chromium scales the document | Find the overflowing box, constrain it (`max-width`, `min-width: 0`), keep `overflow: hidden` on `html, body` | | Content overflows into the margin band | Element taller than the page area | Shorten the block, or reduce its font size via a scoped CSS rule | | Text is unreadable over a photo | No solid field behind the words | Move the text, bound the photo, or use the scoped contrast fix for body copy | | Image placeholder says "Image unavailable" | Search returned nothing usable | Use a simpler, more literal query; or supply `img:` / a direct URL | | Sourced photo is irrelevant | The query was abstract, or ranking rewarded size | Review the contact sheet and pin `search:commons:` | | Chart labels overlap | Long category names | The renderer switches to horizontal bars past 13 characters; shorten labels or use fewer series | | TOC page numbers wrong | Content shifted between passes | Rebuild; the two-pass scan re-reads the final PDF | | Page number duplicated in the TOC | Heading text repeated on another page | Make the heading unique, or set `toc_depth: 1` | | Blank page at the end | Trailing break or margin collapse | Remove the trailing blank line or `page-break` | | Table split badly | More than 9 rows | Expected: long tables split with repeating headers, or shorten | | Metadata is empty | A merge or export path dropped it | Finalize with PyMuPDF `set_metadata` and save with `garbage=3`; do not merge PDFs with pypdf | | PDF is not tagged | A merge or intermediate save dropped `StructTreeRoot` | Render cover and body as one Chromium document; avoid merging | | Font missing / fallback | Custom font not installed | Use theme fonts, or embed via `@font-face` in a custom CSS file | --- ## 10. Definition of done - [ ] The PDF opens and every page has a purpose. - [ ] The cover names the document and the reader, not just the topic. - [ ] Contents page numbers are correct, or there is deliberately no TOC. - [ ] Numbers appear as metrics or charts, not only in sentences. - [ ] Images are relevant, credited, and not stretched. - [ ] No blank, stranded, or half-empty pages. - [ ] Headers, footers, and page numbers are consistent. - [ ] Previews were inspected after the final build. - [ ] `check` reports body type at the declared size, text at or above 9pt, and a line measure inside the target range. - [ ] `check` reports `/Lang`, a structure tree, and an outline. - [ ] Contrast was probed after the final build and every issue is fixed or deliberately accepted. Deliver with the absolute output path and a short statement of page count, contents, and the measured result. Do not claim the document is finished before looking at it. ---
title: "Supplai — Developer Handover"
subtitle: "Peer-to-peer medicine stock sharing for Nigerian PHCs · architecture + phase 1 + rules"
author: "Supplai team"
org: "Supplai"
client: "GBSN Social Logistics Challenge 2026 — Health track"
date: "2026-11-02"
version: "1.0"
summary: "What a second developer needs to know before touching any code — the one idea (confirm before dispatch), the architecture (five boxes, you own the middle), the data model (append-only ledger), the non-negotiable rules (two ledgers, short TTL, no patient data, SMS-only), and the six-week build plan."
confidential: "Internal — build team"
theme: midnight
scenario: pitch-deck
page_size: A4
landscape: false
toc: true
toc_depth: 2
cover_image: "img:assets/okada-rider-called-passenger.jpg"
cover_caption: "A motorcycle rider — the delivery layer. The photo is atmosphere of the system's world, not our own."
back_cover:
  title: "Confirm before you dispatch."
  text: "The architecture, the rules, the six weeks — all in one brief. Read DEV-BRIEF.md, then build the loop."
---

# Supplai — Developer handover

**Status:** architecture decided, nothing built yet.  
**For:** the second developer joining the build.  
**Read next:** `report.md` (the evidence), `PRODUCT.md` (the pitch), `supplai_deck.html` (the deck we've already shown judges), this file (the build plan).

---

## 1. The one idea

**Confirm before dispatch.** The clinic that is about to receive medicine must check its *physical shelf* and reply before a rider moves stock.

We are not building an inventory system, a pharmacy, a delivery company, or a marketplace — three of those exist in Nigeria and are better funded. We are building the thin piece that connects them: request → match → shelf-confirm → rider → proof → two records that agree.

Why it is the architecture: Nigerian LMIS inventory accuracy runs 70–87%. If we dispatch on the database, roughly one in four trips is wasted — the "surplus" isn't there, the rider burns fuel, and the receiving clinic stops trusting the network forever. The database may *suggest*; only a human at the shelf may *commit*.

Three consequences we must not design away:

- A match is **not** a commitment. It is an invitation to check.
- Confirmation has a short life (10 minutes). A yes from this morning is worthless this afternoon.
- Two clinics may confirm the same surplus at once. Exactly one may win.

Get those right and the rest is CRUD.

---

## 2. Phase 1 — one vertical slice

| Dimension | Phase 1 |
|---|---|
| Geography | One LGA. 8–12 facilities. |
| Drugs | 2–3 ambient-stable tracer items (not oxytocin — cold-chain excluded; decide before pilot) |
| Channel | SMS only. No app, no USSD, no WhatsApp. |
| Riders | 2–4 contracted okada, paid per verified drop |
| Records | CSV import from existing bin cards / OpenLMIS export |
| Dashboard | Read-only, one LGA officer, daily |

**Definition of done:** Facility A texts → B confirms shelf → rider delivers → receiver enters code → both stock records change → LGA officer sees it the next morning, without anyone calling her.

---

## 3. What not to build (yet)

Each is a month. Don't build them now.

- Mobile app (SMS is the product)
- National drug database (seed 40, grow from requests)
- Payments inside the channel (money by bank / mobile-money; keep the SMS clean)
- Cold chain / vaccine
- Patient data of any kind (facilities, drugs, quantities, times — only)
- AI (fuzzy match is `pg_trgm`; explainable to a regulator)
- Public→private stock movement (see §7 — the one rule that kills the company)

---

## 4. Architecture — five boxes, you own the middle

```
Feature phone (nurse) —SMS—►  SUPPLAI CORE  ◄—API—  Fleetbase (riders, tracking, proof)
                                  │
                    ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
                    ▼                           ▼
            Africa's Talking              OpenBoxes / OpenLMIS
            shortcode, reverse-billed      stock records (import first)
```

**Stack recommendation:** TypeScript + Fastify + PostgreSQL 16, or Django + DRF + PostgreSQL. One language, one framework. Postgres specifically: `pg_trgm` for fuzzy matching; row-level security for LGA-scoped dashboards.

---

## 5. Data — append-only, never derive a balance

```sql
facility (id, name, type, lga_code, ledger, phone_primary, pcn_licence)
drug     (id, canonical_name, rxnorm_cui, cold_chain, active)
drug_alias (alias, drug_id, source)
stock_level (facility_id, drug_id, qty, as_of, source)  -- CACHE
request  (id, facility, drug_id, qty, raw_text, status, created_at, expires_at)
match    (id, request_id, facility_id, qty_offered, status, confirmed_at, confirm_expires_at)
transfer (id, request_id, match_id, from, to, drug_id, qty, rider_id, dispatch_code, status)
stock_movement (id, transfer_id, facility_id, drug_id, delta, reason, recorded_at, recorded_by)  -- TRUTH
message_log (id, direction, phone, body, provider_id, received_at, processed_at, error)
```

**Non-negotiable rules:**

- `stock_level` is a cache; `stock_movement` is truth. Rebuild from ledger.
- `transfer` only from `confirmed` + not-expired `match`.
- `delta` signs fixed: giver negative, receiver positive. Wrong signs are silent bugs — write a test.
- `message_log` keeps misspellings. It improves matching and proves what was said.

---

## 6. The SMS flow (exact)

Africa's Talking shortcode, **reverse-billed**, idempotent on `provider_id`.

```
09:14 A → shortcode  NEED OXY 20
09:15 shortcode → B  "Supplai: A PHC needs 20 oxytocin 10IU. On shelf now? YES 20 / NO — Ref 4471"
09:19 B → shortcode  YES 20
09:20 shortcode → A  "Rider coming. Code 8842. Ref 4471"
10:02 A → shortcode  8842
10:02 shortcode → A, B  "Delivered. Records updated."
```

**Implementation notes:** normalize `0803...` / `+234803...` to E.164; trust gateway `received_at`; never let old messages resurrect dead requests; parse `YES` / `Y 20` / `yes 20.` in one pass (no punctuation required); one clarifying reply then expire.

---

## 7. The two-ledger rule (the one that kills the company if broken)

`facility.ledger = 'public'` (PHCs, LGA stores) vs `'private'` (licensed pharmacies). **Transfer valid only when `from.ledger == to.ledger`.** Enforce in DB trigger + test. If public stock flows into a pharmacy, you've built a diversion channel with a receipt.

Pharmacies still participate — they pay subscriptions, receive from pharmacies, deliver to clinics as *riders*. Never as recipients.

---

## 8. Matching (simple, not smart)

```sql
SELECT drug_id FROM drug_alias WHERE alias % $1 ORDER BY similarity DESC LIMIT 3;
```

GIN index on `alias gin_trgm_ops`. Threshold ≥ 0.45 only if top beats second by margin. Else ask one disambiguating question. Never invent a drug — loud failure is safer than silent wrong match.

---

## 9. Reservations and races (Tuesday's problem)

Confirmation → `reserved` with `confirm_expires_at = now() + 10 min`. Take with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`; check row count. If unused, `reserved → offered` once, then `expired`. Dispatch → `reserved → consumed`. Write a test that runs concurrent confirmations and asserts exactly one `transfer`. Do it a hundred times.

---

## 10. Proof of delivery

Four-digit code, generated at dispatch, sent to receiver, entered by receiver. Rider never sees it; rider cannot confirm. Two attempts, then lock and flag for human. If receiver has no phone, supervisor enters in dashboard — log who.

---

## 11. Records integration (two phases, deliberately)

- **Phase 1:** nightly CSV import from OpenLMIS/OpenBoxes or photographed bin card → our `stock_level`. We write movements back as CSV for manager to paste. Ugly, honest, ships week 3.
- **Phase 2:** OpenLMIS REST API. Map our `stock_movement` to its event. Keep our ledger authoritative for our transfers. **Do not attempt bidirectional real-time sync in phase 1.** Reconciliation bugs eat timelines.

---

## 12. Dashboard (one screen, read-only)

- Stockouts by facility/drug, hours open
- Transfers in flight
- Unmet requests (the subscription case)
- Response rate per facility
- Row-level security on `lga_code`

---

## 13. Testing that catches the real failures

| Test | Protects |
|---|---|
| Duplicate webhook replay | Double dispatch / double movement |
| Two concurrent confirms | Over-allocation |
| Expired confirmation used | Stale-shelf dispatch |
| `YES` variants | Nurses locked out |
| Typo corpus (50 real misspellings) | Wrong drug |
| Ledger sign test | Silent balance error |
| Cross-ledger attempt | Diversion |
| Clock skew (old message) | Resurrection of dead request |

Keep real gateway payloads from pilot week 1 as fixtures forever.

---

## 14. Security / privacy / operations

- No patient data. Enforce via schema review, not policy.
- Phone numbers = personal data (NDPA 2023). Encrypt, restrict, delete on request.
- Rate-limit inbound SMS; dead-letter queue; kill switch that stops outbound SMS.
- Structured logs with `request_id` through every step.
- Alert: webhook failure > 1%, unmatched drug > 10%, confirmation < 30%.

---

## 15. Order of work (six weeks)

| Week | Ship |
|---|---|
| 1 | Schema, drug seed, webhook, message log, one facility |
| 2 | Request → match → offer → confirm (with TTL + race tests) |
| 3 | Dispatch, proof, ledger writes — end-to-end sandbox |
| 4 | CSV import, read-only LGA dashboard |
| 5 | Two riders, one LGA, two drugs, supervised |
| 6 | Measure top three failures; final handover |

**Rule:** ship week 3 before making week 4 pretty. A working ugly loop beats a beautiful broken one.

---

## 16. Traps (the ten you will hit)

1. Optimising matching before real messages exist.
2. Treating confirmation as formality.
3. Letting "yes" live for hours.
4. Building for the smartphone you own.
5. Making the nurse pay anything (must be reverse-billed).
6. Confusing rider's phone with receiver's confirmation.
7. Adding public→private edge "just for pilot".
8. Deriving balances (rebuild from ledger).
9. Silent failures wherever parsing / matching / dispatch fails.
10. Scope creep into inventory management.

---

## 17. How to work with us

- Bring a decision, not a question: *"I'm doing X because Y, unless you say otherwise."*
- Small PRs, one behaviour each.
- Confirmation / reservation / ledger logic gets a test in the same PR.
- If the deck and the data disagree, data wins — tell us.

---

*The pitch is done (9 slides, `supplai_deck.html` + `.pptx`, both verified). What is left is the boring, correct version of one loop, in one LGA, for two drugs. That is the whole job.*

- Testing: webhook replay, concurrent confirms, sign test on ledger, typo corpus, clock-skew resurrection — fixtures kept from pilot week 1.
